heroHeadline: IDF Kills Khan Younis Criminal Police Chief and Aide as Gaza Ceasefire Continues to Erode — Cumulative Toll 873+
heroSubtitle: Israeli airstrikes on May 10, 2026 killed at least three Palestinians in Gaza, including Khan Younis criminal police chief Wessam Abdel-Hadi and his aide in the Al-Amal neighborhood, and one person in the Maghazi refugee camp — bringing the cumulative Palestinian death toll since the October 10, 2025 ceasefire to 873+. Hamas's Interior Ministry condemned the strike as targeting civil governance in violation of international law. The Israeli military issued no comment. Israel has conducted near-daily strikes throughout the ceasefire, with both sides accusing the other of violations. The broader deadlock persists: Hamas has refused the Board of Peace's five-stage disarmament roadmap, while Israel has indicated it will not withdraw from the 'yellow line' within Gaza. Israel's security cabinet continues to deliberate formally resuming full-scale military operations, with senior military officials pressing for action. The Gaza war death toll since October 7, 2023 now stands at 72,673+ documented, with the true toll including indirect deaths estimated to exceed 90,000–100,000.
footerNote: Data sourced from UN OCHA, IDF, Gaza Ministry of Health, B'Tselem, ICC, ICJ, Reuters, Al Jazeera, OHCHR, UNRWA, Times of Israel, Haaretz, Bloomberg, Jerusalem Post, Human Rights Watch, Save the Children, Amnesty International, and institutional analyses. Casualty figures are subject to ongoing verification. The conflict has persisted since Israeli independence on May 14, 1948.
